LESSON: DIVISION

Grade: Grade 3
Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
Strand: Numbers 1.6 Multiplication By the end of the sub-strand, the learner  Learners 
Topic 1.7: Division

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Division. Read, look at the pictures, practise, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: LOOK AND LEARN

[[image:/media/pupil-books/grade-3/mathematics/page-096.jpg|Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 3 — page 96]]

From your pupil's book (page 96)

Week 9 Lesson 5 Relationship between hour hand and minute hand 1. The clock face has 12 equal divisions marked 1 to 12. 2. Each division between two numbers is an hour 3. Between two numbers are five smaller equal divisions. Each small division is a minute. Activity 1. How many big divisions can you see on the clock face? 2. How many small divisions can you see on the clock face?

Work to do Draw a clock face with 1. Hour hand pointing at 8 and minute hand pointing at 4 2. Hour hand pointing at 11 and minute hand pointing at 6 3. Hour hand pointing at 12 and minute hand pointing at 8 4. Hour hand pointing 3 and minute hand pointing 9 85

[[image:/media/pupil-books/grade-3/mathematics/page-082.jpg|Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 3 — page 82]]

From your pupil's book (page 82)

Division Week 7 Lesson 5 Dividing numbers Example 8÷2= How many can we substract 2 from 8? 8 – 2 – 2 – 2 – 2 = 0 time 8 – 2 = 6 = 1 time 6 – 2 = 4 = 2 times 4 – 2 = 2 = 3 times 2 – 2 = 0 = 4 times We can subtract 2 from 8 four times. 8 ÷ 2 = 4 Work to do Divide

[[image:/media/pupil-books/grade-3/mathematics/page-119.jpg|Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 3 — page 119]]

From your pupil's book (page 119)

Activity Let us read 798, 191, 289, 80, 75,

921, 19, 816, 14, 710. Work to do 1. Learners in pairs or in groups to read number symbols 1 - 1000, both forward and backwards

SECTION 3: TRY THIS

1. Look again at the examples or pictures above.
2. Tell a parent or friend what Division means, using your own words.
3. Copy one example into your exercise book and change it to fit your school or home.
4. Underline three new words and find out what they mean.

SECTION 4: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Division.
2. Complete any “Work to do” items shown in the pupil book pages above.
3. Create three of your own practice questions on this topic.
4. Answer the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after finishing.

SECTION 5: REMEMBER

1. Topic: Division
2. Subject: MATHEMATICS ACTIVITIES
3. Learning materials: Mathematics Pupil Book Grade 3
4. Revise with the quiz now.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
